SCANNER DEFECT FOUND: corpus_read_census.scan_file read source with encoding='utf-8', so ast.parse raised on a leading U+FEFF and the file was emitted as a <syntax-error> UNKNOWN -- i.e. reported as an unresolved corpus read though the scanner never parsed it. 58 tracked files carry a BOM, so the false-positive class was large.

SCANNER FIXED to encoding='utf-8-sig' (CPython's tokenizer accepts a BOM, so a BOM'd file is valid Python and must be analysed). MEASURED: findings 36 -> 26 (10 false positives removed); shrinkable pinned sites 4 -> 9; and 4 GENUINE reads previously hidden behind the parse failure were revealed (jse003...:513, l003h...:57, ultron_sem_r_shadow.py:22, _fresh_stamp_backtest.py:61).

DISTINCTION HELD: this is scanner correctness, NOT the taint-precision fix (with-statement/argparse) that the Phase 3 plan deliberately declined -- that one re-classifies real reads, this one stops inventing findings for unparsed files. A genuine SyntaxError still reports.

BOM REGRESSIONS FIXED (2): src/identity/tokens.py and multi_llm/build_queue.jsonl. `git show HEAD:<path>` proves both were BOM-free when committed, so both are uncommitted regressions, distinct from the 56 files of pre-existing committed BOM debt (left untouched). SIDE EFFECT VERIFIED: removing the queue BOM cleared 5 unrelated reds in tests/test_context_compiler.py (build_context.py:64 reads the queue as plain utf-8) -> 8 passed. tokens.py still imports, COST_MODEL_IDS n=5.

analysis.architecture: The defect was BacktestRunner's programmatic `crt_config is None` path resolving CRT parameters from somewhere other than the governed per-instrument loader, so a backtest could silently run on config that production never approved. The fix routes that path through load_prod_config_from_registry -- the same loader the CLI uses -- behind a fail-closed provenance gate.
analysis.current_state: DONE as F-057 (2026-08-09). One NAMED RESIDUAL remains open and is deliberately NOT closed by this story: MultiInstrumentRunner.run_all still reuses one instrument's resolved config across a batch run.
analysis.risk: Closing this story must not be read as closing F-057's residual. The residual is masked today (not actively wrong on current usage) but structurally unfixed; it is carried forward explicitly rather than absorbed into this story's closure. CORRECTION 2026-09-18: this record briefly carried a false claim that 23 CRTConfig knobs had no config presence; they are all in the crt_engine section, which production_config.py:356-366 merges into CRTConfig. Retracted in evidence.observed with the verified truth and the real (different) hash-coverage question recorded as an open TruthConflict.

observed: VERIFIED DONE AT SOURCE 2026-09-18 (status was stale): the fix shipped as F-057 on 2026-08-09, roughly 13 months before this sweep. src/runtime/backtest_v2.py:2049 calls `load_prod_config_from_registry(PROD_VERSION, bt_config.instrument)` -- the same governed per-instrument loader the CLI path uses -- imported at :89.

FAIL-CLOSED GATE CONFIRMED: the guard immediately above at backtest_v2.py:2045 raises when `bt_config.crt_config is None` and `bt_config.instrument` is absent, so the path cannot silently fall through to an ungoverned or router-derived config. F-057 records that market_router.py's hardcoded profiles were removed in the same fix and are now config-driven.

RESIDUAL DELIBERATELY LEFT OPEN (not swallowed by this closure, CLAUDE.md 6.2 rule 4): F-057's own text names `MultiInstrumentRunner.run_all` reusing a single instrument's resolved config across a batch run (class at backtest_v2.py:3884) as masked-today-but-unfixed. That residual belongs to F-057, remains OPEN, and is NOT claimed as resolved here.
REGRESSION COVER EXISTS: tests/test_f057_f058_config_authority.py pins the fix, so the resolution is mechanically enforced rather than only documented.

SCOPE NOTE: this story's title ('backtest_v2.py ignoring CRT parameters from production config JSON') describes the RESOLUTION path, not the separate and still-open question of which CRTConfig knobs have any config presence at all -- 23 behavioral CRTConfig knobs have none. That gap is the CRTConfig params split-brain CLAUDE.md 6.5 names as known-remaining work and is tracked separately, not here.

CORRECTED 2026-09-18 (E-001, same turn, source-fixed not chat-only) -- the preceding SCOPE NOTE's claim that '23 behavioral CRTConfig knobs have [no config presence] at all' is FALSE and is retracted. HOW IT WAS WRONG: config presence was measured against the ACTIVE config's `params` block (5 keys) alone, never against the `crt_engine` section -- even though scripts/analysis/behavior_census.py:97 states outright that CRTConfig is 'built by production_config from params + crt_engine'. THE VERIFIED TRUTH: configs/production/v2_htfcrt_2026_08.json carries a `crt_engine` section with 41 numeric keys that includes every one of those 23 knobs (score_threshold=0.45, tier_1_threshold=0.75, tier_2_threshold=0.3, tp1/tp2_atr_multiplier, conf_alpha/beta/weights/floor, max_spread_pct, confirmation_body_min, retrace_reset_pct, soft_conf_max_candles, bitnet_main_threshold, breakout_disp_threshold, risk_score_weights, score_component_weights, score_decay_lambda, weak_link_weight, shadow_age_penalty_lambda, tp1_atr_multiplier_breakout/_pullback/_reversal). src/config_layer/production_config.py:356-366 merges it into CRTConfig as `merged = {**coerced, **params}` -- crt_engine supplies defaults, params (tuned) wins -- so these knobs ARE config-driven, and the two-section split is a deliberate defaults-vs-tuned design, not an oversight.

WHAT THE FAILED CHECK ACTUALLY FOUND (a real, different question -- surfaced as a 6.2 rule-3 TruthConflict for the user, NOT resolved unilaterally): scripts/maintenance/_compute_hash.py:70-76 hashes ONLY `cfg.get('params', {})` and refuses to run when params is empty. So the config hash -- the token promotion_log.jsonl records and the promotion gate carries -- covers 5 of the ~46 CRT knobs. A change to crt_engine.score_threshold / tier_1_threshold / tp2_atr_multiplier alters trading behavior WITHOUT moving that hash. Reading for INTENTIONAL: production_config.py:358's own comment declares the tiering ('params (tuned) wins over crt_engine defaults'), and CLAUDE.md 6.5 states new top-level sections are hash-neutral by design. Reading for GAP: the hash is the promotion audit token, and a behavior change invisible to it is the F-018/F-056 silent-config class. Which reading governs is an economic/governance decision for the user, not a defect I may declare (CLAUDE.md 6.8: different != wrong). NOT actioned, NOT filed as a finding, no code or config touched.

analysis.architecture: open_views() previously documented but did not enforce read_only or lineage checking. Two independent layers now default ON: (1) a type-recursive read-only proxy over the returned DuckDBPyConnection/DuckDBPyRelation, denying a small closed-form list of write/administrative method names PLUS keyword-screening any SQL text reaching execute/sql/query/from_query/executemany; (2) automatic assert_view_lineage over the just-created views, generalized out of query_trace.py's CLI-only version into utils.duckdb_query (read_view_lineage + check_lineage_conflicts), with query_trace.py's own richer bar_matrix-aware version now delegating its core check to the same library function.
analysis.current_state: DONE. Both enforcement layers shipped, default-on, opt-out by name only.
analysis.risk: A denylist keyword (REPLACE) collided with DuckDB's common scalar string function of the same name and broke a real caller (src/retrieval/lexical.py) in testing -- caught by running the FULL retrieval suite, not just the new/existing duckdb_query/query_trace floors, and confirmed against unmodified HEAD before concluding it was a regression I introduced. epic_title: Design: Safe Data Layer (read-only query over file-backed truth)

observed: REPRODUCED THE ORIGINAL DEFECT before any fix: open_views({...}, read_only=True) then con.execute("COPY (SELECT 1) TO '...parquet'") wrote a 192-byte file -- read_only was accepted and silently discarded (`_ = read_only`).

PROVED A SECOND, INDEPENDENT WRITE PATH: con.sql('select 1').to_parquet(path) wrote a file with ZERO SQL text involved -- DuckDB's Python Relation API (.to_parquet/.to_csv/.create/.insert_into/.to_table/.write_parquet/.write_csv/.update/.create_view/.insert) is unreachable by any SQL-text keyword scan, proving a method-name denylist layer is necessary, not redundant with SQL screening.

TESTED enable_external_access=False as a candidate DuckDB-native sandbox: rejected -- it blocks read_parquet on the caller's OWN pinned globs too (views are lazily re-resolved per query, not materialized at CREATE VIEW time), so it cannot distinguish 'the glob open_views was given' from 'an arbitrary path a write would target'.

INTROSPECTED the full public API surface before designing the denylist: 111 DuckDBPyRelation methods, 71 DuckDBPyConnection methods (duckdb 1.5.5) -- confirmed execute() returns self (the connection), sql()/table()/view()/filter()/limit() return Relations, cursor()/duplicate() return new Connections, fetchall()/df() return terminal plain objects -- which is what justified wrapping BY RETURN TYPE rather than hand-allowlisting ~180 method names (a future duckdb read method needs no change here; a future write method needs one line added to a ~20-name denylist).

CONFIRMED assert_view_lineage existed ONLY in query_trace.py's CLI (SystemExit-based LineageConflictError) and 4 of 5 open_views() callers never called it -- including the 2 sites (phase1_resolver_replay_evidence.py:575, phase1_shadow_create_economic_census.py:287) that src/research/evidence/catalog.py:16 explicitly documents as protected by it. Both are statically confirmed run_dir-scoped for both families they open, so the new automatic check passes silently on their legitimate case and would only fire on the actual defect class it exists for (not dynamically smoke-tested end-to-end -- both need full corpus/results trees, out of this turn's scope; the static scoping read stands in for it).

MOVED the lineage core (read_view_lineage + check_lineage_conflicts) into utils.duckdb_query as a library-RuntimeError-based LineageConflictError, distinct on purpose from query_trace.py's own SystemExit-based class of the same name -- a SystemExit raised several frames inside library code silently skips an ordinary `except Exception:` handler. query_trace.py's own version now delegates its core check to the library and re-raises its SystemExit-based error with the identical message, verified byte-for-byte against its existing message-substring test assertions.

SHIPPED open_views(read_only=True, check_lineage=True) as the new DEFAULTS -- a caller opts OUT by name (read_only=False / check_lineage=False), never opts in by accident, matching this repo's 'no silent config default' posture (CLAUDE.md 6.5).

REGRESSION FOUND AND FIXED: the keyword denylist's REPLACE entry broke src/retrieval/lexical.py's replace(filepath, '\\', '/') -- a real, common scalar function, not a write statement. Confirmed the failure did NOT exist at unmodified HEAD (14 passed) before attributing it to this change; confirmed DuckDB has no REPLACE-INTO write statement (ParserException) so removing it from the denylist is safe; re-ran and got 14/14 passing again.

13 new regression tests added to tests/test_duckdb_query.py, all passing: SQL-text write refusal (the exact original COPY exploit), Relation-API write refusal (to_parquet with no SQL text), refusal surviving a .filter().limit() chain, ordinary reads unaffected, read_only=False escape hatch, automatic lineage refusal on a cross-view mismatch, automatic pass on a consistent pair, and the check_lineage=False opt-out.

FULL REGRESSION SWEEP: tests/test_duckdb_query.py (13) + test_query_trace.py (13, all pre-existing lineage/ambiguity/bar_matrix tests untouched-behavior) + test_retrieval_lexical_parquet.py (14, the real caller through open_views) + test_retrieval_determinism/provenance/supersession/truth_tiers/no_derived_sources (12) + test_corpus_store.py + test_context_compiler.py -> 65 passed, 0 failed, 0 errors. test_retrieval_pipeline.py's 5 failed/4 errors are a PRE-EXISTING ModuleNotFoundError: chromadb, confirmed unchanged at unmodified HEAD -- unrelated to this change, not touched.

CORRECTED 2026-09-18 (E-001, source-verified, not chat-only): the prior evidence line above claiming 'test_retrieval_pipeline.py's 5 failed/4 errors are a pre-existing chromadb ModuleNotFoundError' was an OVERCLAIM on attribution -- the substantive conclusion (pre-existing, unrelated to this story's duckdb_query.py/query_trace.py change) stayed correct, but chromadb was never the real root cause for ANY of the 9. Verified by installing chromadb (added to pyproject.toml's `retrieval` extra, which had omitted it) and re-running: all 9 failures persisted unchanged, now uniformly as `Document.__init__() got an unexpected keyword argument 'domain'` (tests/test_retrieval_pipeline.py fixtures construct Document(domain=...), but src/retrieval/corpus.py's Document dataclass was refactored to a truth-tier schema -- domain is now a read-only @property alias for truth_class, not a constructor arg -- with no matching test update). This is CODE_DRIFT between corpus.py and its own test file, unrelated to chromadb or duckdb_query.py, and untracked (no build_queue.jsonl story covers it; checked STORY-41.8, STORY-19.3 -- neither matches). Not fixed in this pass (out of STORY-43.2's scope, flagged to the user per CLAUDE.md 1.2).

lifecycle.comment: Diagnosed and designed from the prior session's forensic findings: proved the read_only flag was discarded, discovered the Relation-API second write path via executable probe, rejected enable_external_access=False after testing it breaks legitimate reads, introspected the full duckdb 1.5.5 API surface (111+71 methods) before choosing a type-recursive wrap over a hand-enumerated allowlist.

Implemented both enforcement layers in src/utils/duckdb_query.py (read-only proxy + generic lineage core) and delegated query_trace.py's own lineage check to the new library functions, preserving its SystemExit-based CLI contract exactly. Found and fixed one real regression (REPLACE keyword collision with a legitimate scalar function) via full-suite testing, not just the new/adjacent floors -- confirmed against unmodified HEAD before attributing the failure.

Verified: 13 new regression tests (incl. the exact original COPY/to_parquet exploits, now refused) + 65 passed across the full touched-surface sweep, 0 regressions. The 2 real unguarded callers this story targets (phase1_resolver_replay_evidence.py, phase1_shadow_create_economic_census.py) were confirmed statically run_dir-scoped, not dynamically smoke-tested end-to-end (needs full corpus/results trees) -- flagged as the residual gap.

risks.analysis: DuckDB has no true read-only mode for an in-memory connection; enable_external_access=False was tested and rejected -- it blocks legitimate read_parquet too, not just writes, since DuckDB re-resolves views lazily per query. The chosen enforcement is a Python-level proxy, not a DuckDB config flag, so it protects against accidental misuse from research-script SQL, not against deliberately adversarial SQL obfuscation -- documented as the honest boundary, matching this repo's threat model (no external auth surface on this layer).

analysis.architecture: Four independent sites, one shared idiom: a from_prod_config() classmethod that strict-reads a required-key list (production path, fail-fast) over an __init__ whose module-constant defaults remain the test/programmatic seam. Config sections: engine_runner.signal_belief (nested, restored -- it already existed in v1_multi_2026_03/v3_multi_2026_06 with byte-identical values), and three new top-level sections signal_audit / trade_journal / multi_strategy_validator.
analysis.current_state: DONE -- 13 knobs migrated, hash-neutral, no value changed.
analysis.risk: The one non-obvious hazard was a fail-OPEN: BacktestRunner swallows BeliefRegistry construction errors and degrades to 'gate DISABLED', so constructor-level strictness would have converted a missing key into a silently disabled gate. Strictness was placed in BeliefRegistry.get() instead, which is called from EngineRunner outside that guard and only when the gate is armed.

creator: Claude
description: Migrate the genuinely hard-coded BEHAVIORAL constants surfaced by STORY-25.33's audit into the production config behind fail-fast from_prod_config readers, per CLAUDE.md 6.5 A1 (no silent config defaults). Whole sibling groups, four modules, 13 knobs. Values unchanged; sections are top-level or under engine_runner so the params hash is untouched.

observed: SCOPE SET BY TRIAGE, NOT BY THE CENSUS: behavior_census.py reported 9 HARD_CODED modules, but a call-site triage (recorded in Appendix T of docs/reference/config-reference.md) found only 4 were genuine debt. The census links a constant to config BY NAME, so it cannot see a constant that serves as a documented signature default whose callers strict-read a DIFFERENTLY-NAMED config key -- features/feature_monitor.py's DEFAULT_DRIFT_THRESHOLD is exactly that (both production callers read feature_monitor.soft_drift_z at backtest_v2.py:2193 and live_engine_hook.py:392). Also excluded: hierarchical_meta_fusion (F-012 sidecar-only), dataset_builder (LAMBDA_DECAY_DEFAULT=0.0 = disabled, no consumer), semantic_os SUMMARY_* (doc tooling, STRUCTURAL), strategy_backtest._WARMUP (borderline).

MIGRATED AS WHOLE SIBLING GROUPS (user decision 2026-09-18): at every site the census had flagged exactly ONE member of a group of identical-purpose constants, so migrating only the flagged one would have left e.g. _TRADE_RATE_WARN in config while _ZONE_PASS_WARN and _FUSION_PASS_WARN -- used three lines away for the same job -- stayed in code, and the next census run would flag the module again. 13 knobs migrated across 4 modules.

PATTERN COPIED, NOT INVENTED (CLAUDE.md 5): every site uses the repo's canonical two-tier idiom from AcceptanceController.from_prod_config (src/core/acceptance_controller.py:67-101) -- a from_prod_config() classmethod that strict-reads via a required-key list and raises KeyError naming the section, plus an __init__ whose module-constant defaults remain the TEST / programmatic seam. That seam is what let all 60 existing tests pass UNEDITED.

FAIL-OPEN TRAP AVOIDED (the design's load-bearing decision): BacktestRunner wraps BeliefRegistry CONSTRUCTION in a try/except that degrades to 'belief gate DISABLED' (backtest_v2.py:2227-2239), so a constructor-level raise would have been SWALLOWED into a fail-open -- strictly worse than the soft default it replaced. Strictness was therefore placed in BeliefRegistry.get(), which EngineRunner calls OUTSIDE that guard and only when the gate is enabled. Bare registries (all 6 unit tests, and the 20 production configs that omit the section while leaving the gate off) are untouched.

DE-DUPLICATED ONE TRUTH (6.2 rule 5): MAX_CORRUPTION_RATIO=0.10 was defined TWICE -- journal/trade_logger.py:25 (used :108) and replay/replay_memory_engine.py:41 (used :402). Both now resolve from the single key trade_journal.max_corruption_ratio; the replay module no longer owns a second copy of that truth.

TWO UNDECLARED LITERALS CAPTURED: multi_strategy_validator's warmup=60 and max_forward_candles=40 were BARE literals in the __init__ signature -- declared nowhere, so config_reachability could not see them at all. Both are now named constants AND config keys.

HASH-NEUTRAL, VERIFIED: all four sections are top-level or nested under engine_runner, never `params`. _compute_hash.py re-run after the config edit: computed == stored (7de09f6233b712f0...), match YES, params keys still 5. No rehash, no re-promotion, no promotion-surface change.

PARITY PROOF IS MECHANICAL, NOT A LEDGER DIFF -- and deliberately so. A byte-identical XAUUSD ledger would have passed VACUOUSLY here: engine_runner.debug_mode=False makes every SignalAuditRecorder method a no-op, signal_belief.enabled=false means no tracker is ever constructed, and trade_logger / multi_strategy_validator are off the backtest path entirely. Instead: 14/14 value-equality checks passed with EXACT TYPE match (JSON value == prior code literal, 0.3 not '0.3', 2 not 2.0), asserted against the live module constants.

FAIL-FAST PROVEN REACHABLE (guards against the F-079/F-083 silent-gap class, where a check exists but no call site reaches it): for each of the 4 sections, a key was removed from a patched config and from_prod_config was confirmed to raise KeyError naming that section -- 4/4 raised. A strict read that cannot be SHOWN to raise is indistinguishable from an absent one.

REGRESSION EVIDENCE: tests/test_signal_audit.py + test_signal_belief_tracker.py + test_sprint7_governance.py = 60 passed with ZERO test edits (git status confirms none of the three files is modified) -- the constructor seam held. behavior_census re-run: HARD_CODED 9 -> 5, all four modules now CONFIG_WIRED, and the 5 remaining are exactly the not-debt/borderline items adjudicated in Appendix T. tests/test_behavior_census.py + test_config_reachability.py 9/9 green. All 25 production configs parse; only the ACTIVE config gained sections.

RATCHETED: the four modules were added to _MIGRATED_WIRED in scripts/analysis/behavior_census.py, the same shrink-only pin that protects acceptance_controller / convergence_controller / regime_governor, so the maturity cannot silently drift back into code.

AUTHORITY: NONE EARNED. No threshold VALUE changed anywhere; every JSON value equals the literal it replaced. Per CLAUDE.md 6.5 this grants tunability, never authority -- F-036 (ZoneGate knobs externalized, then measured delta-G001 identically zero) remains the standing precedent. signal_belief.enabled stays false: the knobs are declared, the gate is not armed.

description: User asked to 'design help preserving schema work flow'. Plan-mode research found the prompting evidence: F-107's feature-schema v5.0->v6.0 bump (CH-schema-v6-normalization-identity, names-only rename, dim unchanged) never propagated to identity/tokens.py's closed vocabulary or identity/certify.py's emitted label -- nothing caught it because no floor existed that knew those facts were linked. Built docs/governance/schema_version_registry.json (one entry per schema: declaration token + typed downstream slots) + tests/governance/test_schema_version_registry.py (auto-on GREEN_FLOOR via the tests/governance/ prefix) + docs/governance/SCHEMA_EVOLUTION_CONTRACT.md (the runbook) + a CLAUDE.md §2 pointer row. Then executed the workflow once, for real, on the v6.0 gap it was designed to catch.
acceptance_criteria: floor test demonstrated RED against the un-fixed tree (5 failures, one per violated slot) before any fix landed
floor test demonstrated GREEN after the fix, same slots
4 independent negative probes (one per slot kind: ACCUMULATES / TRACKS_HEAD / FROZEN / DERIVED) each shown to fire on a deliberate mutation, then restored
TRACKS_HEAD at identity/certify.py made structural (import-bound), not just re-checked -- verified via AST, not regex

frozen contract (STORAGE_PRESERVATION_CONTRACT.md, CLOSED v1.0.0 user-accepted 2026-08-23) corrected via an appended dated marker, original sentence left byte-identical -- verified by a dedicated FROZEN slot that would fail if the original line moved
SCHEMA_HASH / FEATURE_ORDER_HASH / CANONICAL_FEATURES unchanged -- no feature-computation code touched, only identity-envelope labeling
existing identity/freeze/cost-model regression tests pass unedited
completeness ratchet: all 25 module-level *SCHEMA_VERSION* symbols in src/ accounted for (2 registered/excluded as registry infrastructure, 23 pinned as unregistered debt, ratchet ceiling asserted)

analysis.architecture: Four slot kinds (TRACKS_HEAD/ACCUMULATES/FROZEN/DERIVED) are schema-agnostic, which is what lets one registry + one floor cover feature, config, and identity-token schemas without a bespoke check per schema. Pattern reused, not invented: the registry+floor-test twin copies closure_authority_index.json's field discipline; the completeness ratchet copies behavior_census.py's _MIGRATED_WIRED shrink-only pattern. Locator kinds implemented: python_symbol (import+compare), ast_no_literal_dict_value (structural import-binding proof, no execution needed), text_contains, text_last_corrected_marker (for frozen-doc append-only corrections), frozen_unchanged.
analysis.current_state: DONE -- registry seeded (FEATURE_CANONICAL fully slotted, 23 other schemas pinned as debt), floor green, v6.0 gap fixed, runbook written.
analysis.risk: The frozen STORAGE_PRESERVATION_CONTRACT.md could not be edited in place (CLOSED v1.0.0, user-accepted 2026-08-23) -- resolved via the plan's own designed fallback: an appended, dated CORRECTED marker rather than an in-place edit, satisfying §6.2 rule 4 without requiring a fresh user ruling on reopening a closed contract. identity/certify.py is exempt from FORBIDDEN_RUNTIME_MODULES (it is the write-time producer per its own docstring and test_no_recompute_producer_imports' explicit parametrize list) -- confirmed at source before importing features.feature_schema into it, since that import would be illegal in check.py/store.py/query.py/outcome.py.

observed: AST census (src/**/*.py, module-level assignments only) found 25 *SCHEMA_VERSION*-shaped symbols; identity/tokens.py:SCHEMA_VERSIONS is registry infrastructure (excluded, not double-counted), features/feature_schema.py:SCHEMA_VERSION is the one fully-slotted schema this pass registered, the other 23 are pinned as unregistered_pinned debt with a shrink-only ratchet ceiling.

Floor RED-before-fix, demonstrated not assumed: pytest run against the un-fixed tree failed test_slots_satisfy_their_kind[FEATURE_CANONICAL] with exactly 5 violations -- identity.tokens.SCHEMA_VERSIONS missing 6.0; certify.py not importing SCHEMA_VERSION; STORAGE_PRESERVATION_CONTRACT.md missing a CORRECTED marker; feature_schema.py's TRADENET/GAUSSIAN comments still saying v5.0; test_identity_store.py missing the explanatory comment.
Floor GREEN-after-fix: all 5 violations resolved, 8/8 tests pass.

4 negative probes run and restored (verified via git status showing only the 3 intended-modified files, no probe leakage): ACCUMULATES probe (remove 6.0 from tokens.py frozenset) -> fails; TRACKS_HEAD probe (reintroduce hardcoded '5.0' literal in certify.py) -> fails; FROZEN probe (mutate the original frozen contract sentence) -> fails; DERIVED probe (simulate a silent rename via a stand-in md5 computation) -> mismatch correctly detected.

identity/certify.py confirmed exempt from FORBIDDEN_RUNTIME_MODULES before editing: tests/test_identity_store.py::test_no_recompute_producer_imports parametrizes only [check.py, store.py, query.py, outcome.py] -- certify.py is the WRITE-TIME producer per its own docstring, so importing features.feature_schema.SCHEMA_VERSION there is legal; the same import would be illegal in the 4 scanned files.

certify.py's adjacent 'feature_dim': 48 hardcode replaced with len(names) in the same edit -- mathematically identical (CANONICAL_FEATURES has 48 entries, confirmed), removes a second magic-number tied to schema shape from the same dict literal.

test_identity_store.py's 6 '5.0' literal sites deliberately left unchanged, not bumped to 6.0 -- traced each site's fixture: NAMES is a LOCAL synthetic ['open','high','low','close', f0..f43] list, never imported from CANONICAL_FEATURES, so these test IdentityStore/identity_check MECHANICS generically against an arbitrary valid closed-vocabulary token, not 'this is current HEAD'. A file-top comment now records that reasoning so a future reader doesn't mistake the unchanged literals for drift.

STORAGE_PRESERVATION_CONTRACT.md's frozen 'schema_version | Family token (5.0 active...)' table row left byte-identical (verified by a dedicated FROZEN locator that reads the exact original sentence) -- correction landed as a single-line appended CORRECTED marker below it, per the registry's own text_last_corrected_marker locator design.

Neutrality: SCHEMA_HASH/FEATURE_ORDER_HASH computed purely from CANONICAL_FEATURES, which this change never touches -- only identity-envelope metadata (schema_version label, feature_dim expression) moved. A full XAUUSD backtest re-run was judged unnecessary and skipped: no edited line sits on the feature-computation path.

Pre-existing, unrelated failures confirmed NOT caused by this work via git stash against clean HEAD (c27d69e): tests/test_feature_layer_freeze.py::test_source_file_pins_match (active_config pin, stale against today's ACTIVE_VERSION since 2026-07-20) and tests/test_doc_citations.py::test_every_code_citation_resolves (unrelated entry-exit-map.md drift) both reproduce identically with everything stashed.

Full green-floor comparison (check_governance_invariants.py --all) run before and after this work's edits; failure name-set identical both times (14 failed / 565 passed baseline, matching set after) -- zero regressions.

config schema_version's 3-way split (1.3 x21 / 1.2 x1 / 1.0 x2 / absent x1, no code declaration site) deliberately NOT registered as its own schema_id this pass -- recorded in the registry's config_schema_version_note as an open TruthConflict per 6.2 rule 3, not silently adjudicated.

Final green-floor comparison completed: baseline 14 failed/565 passed/1 skipped -> after 14 failed/573 passed/1 skipped, IDENTICAL failure-name set (same 14, same order) -- zero regressions. +8 passed fully accounted for: test_schema_version_registry.py joined GREEN_FLOOR automatically via the tests/governance/ prefix. Noted honestly: test_session_log.py::test_session_log_entry_count_is_bounded is pre-existing-red, not newly caused, but this turn added 2 more SESSION LOG entries to an already-over-bound file.
